newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KPW head sees 1997 offers worth $1.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Polish KPW head sees 1997 offers worth $1.5 bln.

text.p: Polish firms should focus on listing on the Polish bourse, where the value of offers in 1997 should reach about $1.5 billion, rather than foreign markets, the Securities Commission (KPW) head said.

"I think that for the time being Polish firms shouldn't leave the Polish market," Jacek Socha told a news conference on Tuesday. He said Polish firms would be less visible on foreign bourses and would benefit more from a Polish listing.
"By the end of the year we should have a sum which should increase the capital on the market by $1.5 billion," he added.

The new securities trading bill passed by parliament's lower house in early June allows Polish firms to float up to 25 percent of shares abroad without the Securities Commission's permission, either directly or through depositary receipts.
The bill could come into force in less than two months.

Socha said that from the start of this year to May 15 the total value of offers on the Polish capital market, not including mass privatisation National Investment Funds (NFIs) and large Bank Handlowy, had reached about 1.44 billion zlotys.
He said that sum was already the highest annual sum in the history of the Polish capital market.
